To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a compression scheme that is specifically tailored for the decoding on the GPU, that achieves a compression factor of 9 for restricted quadtree models, that allows for efficient streaming of large DEMs from disk into GPU memory, that allows for sustained rendering throughput of over 300 million triangles, that achieves a frame rate of over 100 FPS for high resolution DEMs, and that allows for scalable rendering with respect, e.g., to screen resolution.
the combination of adaptive triangulation, quadtree based compression, and GPU based decoding is an efficient approach to the rendering of large scale digital terrain models.
the presented geometry compression scheme is efficient for realtime terrain rendering on the GPU.
In summary, our research is concerned with
efficient GPU based decoding of large terrain models for realtime visualization.
the design of a geometry compression scheme that enables the efficient streaming of large DEMs from main to GPU memory for real time terrain rendering.
the design of efficient compression schemes that are tailored to GPU based decoding, and with the design of storage formats for compressed data on the GPU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented method is very fast and can be applied in realtime rendering.
the method is a good compromise between compression and speed, but not the best of both.
the proposed method allows for a significant increase in rendering performance for large DEMs on high resolution displays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed scheme enables realtime visualization of large DEMs with a high level of detail, even on high end GPUs.
we present the first realtime terrain rendering system for large DEMs that can be adapted to any display resolution.
we can render a DEM with 2 5 billion triangles on a 4K monitor with a maximum screen space deviation of one pixel at more than 100 fps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GPU based rendering is a viable alternative to CPU based rendering for large DEMs.
it is possible to render very large DEMs at interactive frame rates by using GPU memory for data buffering and by exploiting the GPU’s massive parallelism for decoding.
GPU based decoding can be used to efficiently render large DEMs at interactive rates on high resolution displays.
